the_ruling_verbatim: we are just going to attach that to the same ticket as a bug we fix with it.
now_the_spec_says: A defect a voyage uncovers is attached to that voyage's ticket and fixed by it. The bounds widen by the ruling; the berthed chart packets do not move — the widening is recorded forward, in the ruling and the verdict's findings, never backward.
context:
THE FULL SPEC SENTENCE, which the door caps at 280: A defect a voyage UNCOVERS is attached to that voyage's ticket and fixed by it, rather than raised as a separate ticket and left standing. The bounds widen by the ruling; the chart berths do not move. This is the disposition for the case where a build's own instrument exposes a pre-existing fault in code the chart never surveyed: the chain said what was known on the day it was charted, and rewriting constrain's bounds.in after the fact would make the record lie about what the chart knew. So the widening is recorded FORWARD — in this ruling, in the verdict artifact's findings against the constrain leg, and in the ticket — never backward into a berthed packet. Applied first to ticket 1c4ae8f053fe, whose cheaper instance seal turned a hollow green red in cairn/devices/inference_domain/probes/an_inference_call_logs_that_it_started.py; the probe fix and the tooth tightening are that ticket's work, not a successor's.

MEASURED, and the measurement is what raised the question. Ticket 1c4ae8f053fe stopped copying the ~/.cairn trail tree into the tester's sandbox (888.7MB/9.28s per sealed proof down to 118.0MB/0.34s). The whole-corpus re-seal sweep then read 200 proofs, 192 green, 8 red. Attribution was measured rather than argued: the working tree was stashed, HEAD c9db255dab8d confirmed to carry the old two-copy isolation.py, and all 8 reds re-run there — 7 are red at HEAD too. The 8th, cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_an_inference_call_logs_that_it_started.py::test_the_probe_reads_the_address_the_device_declares, was green at HEAD and red under the new seal.

THE DIAGNOSIS: survey_the_corpus resolves the trail through TWO doors and only the first follows the device. Line 143 asks domain.diagnostic_trail(), which honours _diagnostic_roots and therefore moves when a proof moves the device's world, and sets trail_exists from it. Line 148 then builds BreadcrumbLog('inference_domain', 0) with NO roots, re-deriving the LIVE logs berth, and reads the records from there. So trail_exists describes the fixture trail and post_era_lines/trail_misses describe the live one. The tooth writes ONE line into an isolated trail and asserts trail_misses >= 1 — it has been passing on the live trail's historical lines, never on the line it wrote. That is verbatim the failure the function's own docstring says it exists to prevent: 'if the device's berth ever moves, a probe carrying its own copy of the address goes on reading an empty directory and reports a catastrophe that is really a stale constant.' Three measurements pin it: sealed at HEAD green, sealed in the working tree red (trail_exists=True, post_era_lines=0, trail_misses=0, store_misses=1794), UNSEALED in the working tree green. The empty logs tree did not break the proof; it removed the accident the proof was passing on.

THE QUESTION PUT TO HIM was whether to fix it (outside 1c4ae8f053fe's constrain bounds, and /sail step 2 says wanting something out is his question, never a silent widening), to rule the criterion charitable and cross PROVED, or to cast the defect as its own ticket. He ruled the first, and attached it to the same ticket.

WHY THE VERDICT DOOR FORCED THE ASK: the chart's criterion 'no proof depended on the old copy' was recorded FAILED rather than read charitably, and cairn/devices/codemother/machines/verdict refuses to BERTH a failed criterion at all — 'a failed criterion is a kick-back, not a crossing.' So the kick-back was physics, not judgement, and it is what surfaced the ruling.

THE FIX THIS AUTHORISES, ~10 lines across three files, each mirroring code within a few lines of it: (1) a diagnostic_records() sibling to diagnostic_trail() in cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py, using the same roots=getattr(self, '_diagnostic_roots', None) that diagnostic_trail already uses at line 212 and _receiver at 247 — diagnostic_trail answers WHERE the records are and nothing answered WHAT they are, which is why a caller re-derived the address by hand; (2) a three-line passthrough in inference_domain/domain.py beside the four already there; (3) the probe reading domain.diagnostic_records() instead of building its own BreadcrumbLog. A grep of every hand-built BreadcrumbLog( in the corpus finds this probe is the ONLY caller omitting roots=.

AND THE TOOTH TIGHTENING IS THE LESSON, not the code fix: the tooth asserts trail_misses >= 1 after writing exactly one line, and >= 1 is what let it pass on the live trail's hundreds of borrowed lines. == 1 could never have — the fixture has one line and the live trail has many, so the assertion would have failed the day the probe was written. A bound that admits the accident is a bound that will be met by the accident.

TRACES TO: Law 8 (a hollow green gets leaned on by a peer, which is why it is worse here than a red); Law 9 (the criterion was recorded failed rather than reinterpreted to let the crossing through); Law 3 (attribution measured at HEAD, not reasoned about); CP1.
confirmation_verbatim: agreed on all counts. ruled approved and boogied
